title: Remove a loaded drawer from ball-bearing slides by pressing both disconnect levers at once
instruction: Take the red-tab drawer completely out of the chest and set it level on the table. Keep its sealed box inside and both jars intact. The target jar may stand upright on the table outside cabinets. Release the drawer for one second.
context: Taking a drawer off full-extension ball-bearing slides is routine furniture and cabinet service: each slide has a spring-loaded disconnect lever, and the slide stop only lets go while the levers on both sides are pressed at the same time as the drawer is pulled. Unlike a drawer whose anti-pull-out stop is cleared by lifting the front, there is no lift-over catch here: only the two levers disable the stop. The robot must keep both levers pressed while pulling, then carry the loaded drawer out without knocking over or striking the glass jars inside.
setup: World frame in metres, Z up; tabletop at Z = 0.75. Two YAM six-axis arms with parallel grippers start at their ready pose, bases at (0.05, +/-0.30, 0.93) with identity rotation. Each arm sits on a rigid steel floor mount: an 80 x 220 x 920 mm post centred at (-0.15, +/-0.30, 0.46) and a 280 x 220 x 20 mm beam centred at (-0.05, +/-0.30, 0.92) (exact values in candidate/mount.json). On the table are two fixed wooden carcasses with steel runners, channels, stops and hooks, and one empty adjacent slot. The target drawer, centred at (0.20, 0, 0.81), runs on side-mounted steel slides modelled on full-extension ball-bearing slides. Each slide has a red spring-loaded disconnect lever (6 mm travel, 700 N/m, about 4.2 N at full travel); the slide stop is disabled only while both levers are pressed more than 4 mm. The second drawer, centred at (0.20, -0.34, 0.81), runs on bottom-mount runners with orange pinch locks and a rear hook; it is not the target. Each drawer assembly measures 302 x 330 x 105 mm including runners and levers (0.914 kg target, 0.894 kg other) and holds one blue ballasted sealed box, 170 x 56 x 51 mm (0.731 kg in the target drawer, 0.966 kg in the other), and one sealed glass jar, 50 mm diameter and 73 mm tall (0.26 kg each). Friction (simulation estimates): wood 0.5, slide steel 0.15, levers and knobs 1.0, glass and feet 0.6. The cabinet's own frame, used in scoring, maps to the world frame by a 180-degree rotation about Z followed by a translation of (0.42, -0.17, -0.05); its x axis points into the cabinet and the cabinet front face of the target slot is at x = 0.12. Every primitive's size, pose, mass, centre of mass, inertia and material is listed in candidate/fixture.json and candidate/inventory.json.
scoring: Score 0 if either jar is damaged after the first 0.3 s (more than 15 N of force from anything other than the gripper finger pads, a closing speed above 0.3 m/s along the contact normal, or a tilt above 30 degrees), if any object leaves the work area or drops, or if either wrist force stays above 80 N for 0.1 s. Otherwise the current state scores 0.25 when every part of the target drawer, including runner ends and levers, is in front of the cabinet face (cabinet-frame x < 0.12 m), the sealed box is still inside it, and the target jar is either inside the drawer or standing upright on the table, and is not touched by the robot. 0.5 additionally requires the drawer resting on the table: centre within 6 mm of cabinet-frame height 0.835 m and centre at cabinet-frame x < 0. 1.0 additionally requires the drawer level (tilt under 3 degrees) with no robot contact for 1 s. The episode ends on success, on a zero condition or at the step limit, and the state at that moment is scored; earlier progress does not count if the final state no longer meets a condition.
reset_notes: Restore all free bodies and their velocities, lever positions, springs and slide stops, and clear the damage, hold, wrist-force and score history. There is one fixed layout; the episode seed does not change the scene.
fidelity: Rigid geometric approximation of ball-bearing slides with disconnect levers and a loaded drawer; no hardware validation, and no glass fracture or liquid simulation (jar damage is a force, impact-speed and tilt threshold). Feet and torsional friction are approximated. Arm joint torque limits including gravity: 27 N m (joints 1-3), 7 N m (joints 4-6), 40 N per finger. Fixed layout; the scripted demo reads simulator state.
